chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mazi (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not prohibit wine for its name, but He prohibited it for its consequence. So whatever has the consequence of wine, it is wine.
ai.seo_question: Why is wine prohibited in Islam according to the hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'idtirar' (causal reasoning) in Shia jurisprudence, shifting the focus from the physical substance of wine to its intoxicating effect. It serves as the foundational evidence for the prohibition of all intoxicants, regardless of their source or name, by linking the specific ruling of wine to its underlying cause. This logic allows jurists to extend the prohibition to new substances that produce similar effects, ensuring the preservation of mental clarity mandated by Sharia.
